coherence.reasons: Both reach the same answer from near-identical models. X's summary is organised into three pillars (the US is worth entering; only Amazon-led fits the limits; what the board has to accept), and each slide maps to one of them. Its constraint scorecard on slide 3 labels payback "At risk", which matches the later ACoS analysis. Y's hierarchy is also logical and its governing thought usefully embeds the ad-cost condition. But Y's summary first says Amazon-led "meets the board's cash, payback and margin limits" and only two points later says payback fails above 28.6% ACoS with a 32% benchmark, so the headline claim holds only on plan inputs. Y also undercuts itself in places: "most new spend is going to Korean brands" sits beside its own 38.6% share of growth.

judgment.reasons: Both recommend Amazon-led entry with gates, reject retail on the cap, payback and margin floor, and weigh Japan fairly, including that Japan returns more cash at 32% ACoS. X is more direct about the trade-off the board must make: no route reaches $40M within the limits, so reset it to 2031–32 and formally accept that 2030 payback is at risk. X also proposes a $4M cash envelope sized to the combined stress case and a three-part retail gate (20% awareness, $20M Amazon sales at ACoS of 30% or less, about 300 doors within margin headroom). Y's strengths are a tighter ACoS gate at the 28.6% break-even and an explicit Japan fallback; X's review trigger of 32% for two quarters is loose relative to its own break-even. Y softens the ambition gap to "two years late", drops the Amazon-scale condition for retail, and leaves the "switch to Japan" mechanics unspecified. On balance X weighs the trade-offs slightly better.

evidence.reasons: The core numbers match each other and the key in both: $4.73 and $7.55 per unit, B peak of −$20.8M, 4.5% group margin, 28.6% break-even ACoS, the ACoS and tariff grid, and a stall case near $7M. Both check the 4.5 units per door against the awareness bands, reject the $5.2B figure, challenge the correlation and note that two of three Amazon-first peers stalled. X is more careful with the pilot: it notes monthly growth slowed from 16–17% to 8–9% and that the 2027 plan needs 1.8 times the June run-rate. X also gives a break-even under the higher tariff (26.9%) and a realistic-inputs case for B (−$31M). Y makes several unsupported or wrong inferences: growth "never paused, a sign of word of mouth"; "US buyers rate it as Korean buyers do" (no Korean rating is in the pack); "the pilot understates what a full range can do"; and "most new spend is going to Korean brands" against its own 38.6%. Y's treatment of the correlation is more thorough, and it quantifies the halo at $3.98M against $31.6M of retail cost, but that does not offset the looser claims.

revision.reasons: Both keep the CEO's Amazon-first hypothesis with conditions, which is what the key expects, and both raise the retail awareness trigger from 15% to 20% using Table 8. Y has a clean from-and-to slide of three changes and gates ACoS at the break-even rather than assuming 25%. X compares the CEO's draft gate by gate, raises the Amazon-scale trigger from $10M to $20M at ACoS of 30% or less, moves retail timing to 2030 at the earliest, and specifies a 300-door first step. X also explicitly resets the $40M ambition and marks payback as at risk. Y drops the Amazon sales condition altogether and is softer on the ambition. Both are appropriate; X's update is somewhat more complete.

overall.reasons: The two documents rest on the same model and reach the same defensible recommendation, so the difference lies in candour and rigour. X tells the board plainly what it must accept: payback is at risk above 28.6% ACoS (26.9% with the higher tariff), $40M is not reachable by 2030 within the limits, and the pilot's growth is slowing. It turns that into specific decisions: a $4M envelope, guardrails and multi-condition retail gates. Y is equally sound on the central numbers and has a sharper ACoS gate and an explicit Japan fallback. But Y headlines that Option A "meets" payback, softens the ambition gap, and includes several over-read claims about the pilot and the market. X would serve the decision maker better, though not by a wide margin.
